gap: No result ChatGPT got states that at today's Jackery US store prices the Explorer 2000 v2 ($999, 2,042 Wh, 39.5 lb) costs $0.49 per Wh and holds 51.7 Wh/lb, while the Explorer 1500 Ultra the results promote ($1,079, 1,536 Wh, 38.6 lb) costs $0.70 per Wh and holds 39.8 Wh/lb. So the Ultra costs $80 more for 506 Wh less and saves only 0.9 lb.
standout_why: I compared these pages. Notebookcheck's 1500 Ultra launch piece gives only the $1,399 MSRP and the $899 early-bird price, with no weight and no other models. GearBrain's HomePower 1000 Plus V2 review covers one unit (1,024 Wh, 23.8 lb, $749 MSRP) and compares no other Jackery. 10adventures covers the old Explorer 240/500/1500 with no prices. Jackery's own 'What, Why and How Much' blog lists capacities but no prices or weights. TechRadar's 1500 Ultra story only came back as a headline. Pro Tool Reviews and Yahoo returned 403 and could not be read. None of these pages puts cost per Wh or Wh per lb side by side across the current lineup.
decides: For a shopper who does not need waterproofing, the Explorer 2000 v2 at $999 is the value pick in the 1.5 to 2 kWh range: the lowest cost per Wh of the units checked and the second-best Wh per lb after the tiny 300D. The 1500 Ultra makes sense only if its IP65 rating, 1 m drop resistance and 800 W solar input are what you are paying for. For a lighter unit around 1 kWh, the HomePower 1000 Plus v2 (23.8 lb) gives up value ($0.65/Wh) to save weight. The Explorer 1500 v2 ($849, 48.0 Wh/lb, $0.55/Wh) is the middle choice. These are sale prices read on 2026-11-15, and Jackery's page says the 2000 v2 is sold out and on pre-order, shipping Nov 16.

findings.note: $289 ÷ 292 Wh = $0.990/Wh; 292 Wh ÷ 7.5 lb = 38.9 Wh/lb. It costs $80 more than the 300D for 4 Wh more and 2 lb more weight. Its advantage is AC outlets: 2 AC at 300 W, which the 300D's listed ports (USB-C, USB-A, DC) do not include.

findings.note: $1,899 ÷ 3,584 Wh = $0.530/Wh. The 7,168 Wh bundle at $3,199 (https://www.jackery.com/products/jackery-homepower-3600-plus-7168wh) works out to $3,199 ÷ 7,168 Wh = $0.446/Wh. The Black unit is on pre-order, shipping by Nov 22.

findings.label: cost per Wh
findings.note: $3,499 ÷ 5,040 Wh = $0.694/Wh. On pre-order, shipping Nov 28. The store tool also returned $3,499 for the '5000 Plus (10kWh)' listing, which looks like the lowest variant price and not the bundle's, so I did not use it.

unsourced: Explorer 1500 Ultra weight from Jackery's own page or manual: jackery.com returned HTTP 429 to WebFetch, and the Shopify product data has no weight. I used Newsshooter's 38.6 lb instead.
Explorer 1000 Plus weight: Jackery's product page was rate-limited (429), and I ran out of tool budget before trying the manual or a reviewer, so Wh per lb is not computed.
HomePower 1000 v2, HomePower 3600 Plus and Explorer 5000 Plus weights: not in the store product text, and the product pages returned 429.

Explorer 1000 v2 current US price: a Jackery store search for 'Explorer 1000 v2' returned no standalone Explorer 1000 v2 listing. Jackery's blog lists it at 1,024 Wh, while Dealectric's listing names 1,070 Wh, so the capacity needs checking.
